behavior: Use an explicit user song title; otherwise label the song with supplied genre and BPM, including partial known metadata.
Update the chat header and saved-song list from project events and preserve metadata across reloads.
Protect manual and legacy named titles. Fill missing automatic labels from saved production briefs without treating generated plan titles as user names.
Validate metadata against the current user request. Naming is available during planning and does not itself change Ableton.

verification.frontend_production_build: Passed locally and in deployment CI
verification.browser_titles: Local and public-site API-fixture tests passed at 1440px and 390px: automatic names, BPM revisions, explicit song names, manual rename protection, saved list and reload. No page errors or horizontal overflow observed. Screenshots inspected.
verification.browser_test_correction: The first public mobile test typed before new-song creation finished. The test now waits for creation and composer readiness; both public viewport runs passed on rerun. No application change was required.
verification.guided_setup: Existing guided-song workflow passed locally and on the public site at both widths.
verification.public_smoke: Login, signup, password reset, guide and changelog returned 200. Invalid-login validation and protected dashboard redirect passed; no broken Next.js assets observed.
verification.actual_provider: Four real Bedrock cases passed: explicit genre/BPM, explicit song name, instrument name not mistaken for song name, and an uncommitted tempo comparison leaving the title unchanged. No musical tools executed.
verification.provider_schema: An unsupported root anyOf was caught in provider testing and removed before deployment; runtime validation still requires metadata.
verification.deployed_runtime: Pure checks inside the deployed task passed for title updates, discussion-tool availability, explicit-name protection and legacy brief fallback. No customer chats modified or Ableton actions executed.
verification.infrastructure: Frontend and backend release identities match the application commit. Service stable, API healthy, protected routes return 401. Secret references, roles, storage, provider and payment settings preserved; only BEATMIND_RELEASE_SHA changed from task 86.

limitations: Unknown metadata is not guessed. Existing unnamed chats receive a derived label only when saved brief metadata is available. Browser tests use isolated API fixtures, not customer sessions. This release does not constitute an audible music or customer-Mac integration test. Refresh the browser; no Bridge reinstall is needed.
